original_question: Is it consistent that the splitting number s equals the ultrafilter number u and still every 2-coloring of s×ω admits a monochromatic rectangle of sizes s and ω, i.e. \( inom{s}{\omega} 	o  inom{s}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\)?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.4: "Is it consistent that \(\mathfrak{s}=\mathfrak{u}\) and still \(\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\)?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target almost exactly. It asks for the same consistency statement as Problem 3.4, keeps the scope at the pair \((\mathfrak{s},\omega)\), and correctly unpacks the arrow notation in terms of 2-colorings of \(\mathfrak{s}\times\omega\) and monochromatic rectangles.
missing_details: State explicitly that \(\mathfrak{s}\) is the splitting number and \(\mathfrak{u}\) is the ultrafilter number.
Say "consistent with ZFC" to make the ambient set-theoretic consistency context explicit.
Name the assertion as the strong polarized partition relation at the pair \((\mathfrak{s},\omega)\).
Spell out the formal quantifiers from Definition 1.1: for every coloring \(c:\mathfrak{s}\times\omega\to 2\), there exist \(A\subseteq\mathfrak{s}\) and \(B\subseteq\omega\).
Specify that \(|A|=\mathfrak{s}\), \(|B|=\omega\), and that "monochromatic rectangle" means \(c\restriction(A\times B)\) is constant.
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that the splitting number \(\mathfrak{s}\) equals the ultrafilter number \(\mathfrak{u}\) and nevertheless the strong polarized partition relation \(\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds; that is, for every coloring \(c:\mathfrak{s}\times\omega\to 2\) there are sets \(A\subseteq\mathfrak{s}\) and \(B\subseteq\omega\) with \(|A|=\mathfrak{s}\) and \(|B|=\omega\) such that \(c\restriction(A\times B)\) is constant?
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact official formulation in Section 3, namely Problem 3.4, not at the neighboring Problems 3.2, 3.3, or 3.5. Definition 1.1 supplies the precise meaning of the polarized-arrow notation, so the stand-alone version should include the explicit coloring formulation. Theorem 2.6 gives the nearby structural context: below the splitting number one already knows when the positive relation holds, so the real issue is the threshold case at \(\lambda=\mathfrak{s}\). The discussion immediately preceding Problem 3.4 says that the known positive model for \(\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) came from a model with \(\mathfrak{u}<\mathfrak{s}=\mathfrak{c}\), which is exactly why the paper asks whether the strict inequality \(\mathfrak{u}<\mathfrak{s}\) is essential.
